Lighter and Lighter on Robinhood Chain expose the
same REST API, WebSocket API and transaction format
. Pick the base URL and chain ID that match the exchange you are integrating; the server selector in each endpoint's
Test it
panel lists the servers that endpoint is available on.

Endpoints marked
Lighter on Robinhood Chain only
(points, referral points) exist only on the RH servers. Endpoints marked
Lighter only
(binary options) exist only on the Lighter servers.
Lighter RH is a
separate exchange
: accounts, balances, API keys, nonces and account indexes don't carry over, and mainnet signatures use distinct chain IDs. The two testnets both use chain ID
300
; keep the base URL and chain ID together instead of relying on chain ID alone to distinguish testnets. See
Lighter on Robinhood Chain
.
Sections
REST API
– almost every endpoint is under
/api/v1/
, grouped by resource. Status (
/
) and info (
/info
) are root endpoints.
WebSocket
– streaming market and account data, and sending transactions over WebSocket.
Explorer API
– blocks, batches, search, statistics, logs by hash, account logs/assets/positions and market logs. The base URLs are
https://explorer.elliot.ai/api
(Lighter) and
https://explorerapi.rh.lighter.xyz/api
(Robinhood Chain).

https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/account/buy.title: POST buyVolumeQuota
https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/account/buy.content:
For the complete documentation index, see
llms.txt
. This page is also available as
Markdown
.
Copy
On this page
Buy volume quota with USDC. Submit a signed L2Transfer of quota × 500 USDC base units to the volume quota payment account; the server validates it, sends it and credits the quota to the payer's L1 address (or destination_l1_address) once the transfer executes. If execution takes longer than about 5 seconds the response is status=pending and the purchase is claimed by calling again with tx_hash. Exactly one of tx_info (new purchase) or tx_hash (claim) is sent per call. Each transfer is credited once. Only Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can receive quota, and the balance after the purchase may not exceed 30,000,000. See
Volume Quota
.
post
https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai
Lighter mainnet
/api/v1/buyVolumeQuota
Header parameters
authorization
string
Optional
Auth token in the Authorization header (or pass auth in the body).
Body
application/x-www-form-urlencoded
quota
integer · int64
Required
Volume quota to buy, in transactions. Price is quota × 500 USDC base units (1,000,000 quota = 500 USDC); at most 15,000,000 per request.
tx_info
string
Optional
Required for a new purchase (omit when claiming with tx_hash). Signed L2Transfer (tx type 12) of USDC (asset index 3), exactly quota × 500 USDC base units from the paying account to the volume quota payment account (index 765210 on Lighter, 51687 on Lighter on Robinhood Chain), as sent to sendTx. Omit when claiming a pending purchase with tx_hash.
tx_hash
string
Optional
Optional; claim only, not needed for a normal purchase. Pass instead of tx_info to finish a purchase whose earlier call answered status=pending: the tx_hash from that response. No new payment is made. Credits that purchase once its transfer has executed; the payer must authenticate.
destination_l1_address
string
Optional
Credit this L1 address instead of the payer's own. Must be a Plus or Premium/Advanced account's L1 address.
auth
string
Optional
Auth token of the paying account (alternatively the Authorization header).
Responses
200
A successful response.
application/json
code
integer · int32
Required
Example:
200
message
string
Optional

string
Required
L1 address the quota is (or will be) credited to.
Example:

Required
Quota credited (status=credited) or to be credited (status=pending).

Balance of the credited L1 address after the purchase. Omitted while pending.

On this page
Lighter only.
Get events and registered order books, including scheduled events with no books. event_ids and market_ids accept up to 50 comma-separated positive IDs, are mutually exclusive, and use the same filters, sorting and pagination. market_ids returns each related event once with all its order books. Defaults to descending id. start_at sorting uses (start_at, event_id); cursor identifies an existing event and excludes it in the requested direction. tag filters across creators; creator_account_index is an optional additional filter. active=true requires a tradeable outcome; active=false includes scheduled and closed events.
Use this endpoint to discover binary options markets and read their actual trading windows, decimals and market fees. Binary options are excluded from
orderBookDetails
. See
Discover markets
for examples, pagination and lifecycle statuses.

On this page
Lighter only.
Get fee tiers. filter=perps|spot returns the regular user tiers (both market types share them). filter=bo returns BO volume tiers and LIT staking discount tiers; filter=all returns everything. An account's BO multiplier is the BO tier fee_rate times the staking fee_rate, applied to each BO market's maker/taker fee (see /api/v1/events) and then scaled by 1 - trade_price / settlement_cap.
Use
filter=bo
to retrieve binary options volume tiers (
bo_tiers
) and LIT staking discounts (
staking_tiers
). Fetch current values rather than hard-coding the tier table.
account limits

Get the OHLC candles (1s = the exact price observations, or 30s) of an up/down market series (symbol + duration, e.g. btc/5m) in a bounded time range (at most 24h), oldest first. Pass next_cursor as start_timestamp to page forward; live candles are on the

Browse guilds and leaderboards, manage your membership, and participate in guild duels.
Guild creation is currently restricted to whitelisted addresses approved by the Lighter team.
Endpoints
Section
Endpoints
Description
Guild discovery
4
Browse guilds, view leaderboards, and look up a guild by referral code.
Membership
3
Check membership, request to join a guild, or leave your current guild.
Duels
5
Browse duel metrics and public duels, or view your guild’s duel details.
Duel actions
4
Challenge another guild, accept or decline a proposal, and report stake transfers.
Requests and authentication
Guilds and Guild Duels are not supported on Robinhood Chain.

Volume quota to buy, in transactions. Price is quota × 500 USDC base units (1,000,000 quota = 500 USDC); at most 15,000,000 per request.
tx_info
string
Optional
Required for a new purchase (omit when claiming with tx_hash). Signed L2Transfer (tx type 12) of USDC (asset index 3), exactly quota × 500 USDC base units from the paying account to the volume quota payment account (index 765210 on Lighter, 51687 on Lighter on Robinhood Chain), as sent to sendTx. Omit when claiming a pending purchase with tx_hash.
tx_hash
string
Optional
Optional; claim only, not needed for a normal purchase. Pass instead of tx_info to finish a purchase whose earlier call answered status=pending: the tx_hash from that response. No new payment is made. Credits that purchase once its transfer has executed; the payer must authenticate.
destination_l1_address
string
Optional
Credit this L1 address instead of the payer's own. Must be a Plus or Premium/Advanced account's L1 address.
auth

On this page
Returns an account's fills grouped by order, with separate entries for each trade type and maker/taker role. Each entry includes total filled size, notional, average price, fees, realized PnL and first/last fill details. Use

This guide covers Lighter mainnet. The endpoint does not require an authentication token.

Timestamp rules:
Both must be on or after the exchange start (Jan 17, 2025 UTC =

If both are set,

Filtering selects stored order aggregates by their last fill time. It does not trim their individual fills to the requested window.
Results are then split by trade type and maker/taker role. Each returned entry's

and

Omitting either timestamp leaves that side of the window unbounded.

Pagination
Stored order aggregates are selected by their overall last trade ID, newest first. Within each order, returned trade-type/role entries are sorted by their own last trade IDs. The flattened response is not necessarily globally sorted by each entry's
last_trade_id
.
If more orders exist, the response includes
next_cursor
. Pass it as
cursor
with the same filters to get the next page. When
next_cursor
is missing, you've reached the end.
limit
counts
orders
. If one order has fills of different
role
or
type
(e.g. part maker, part taker), it comes back as one entry per role/type, so
trades
can contain more entries than
limit
.
Orders still receiving fills can move between requests. A fixed
end_timestamp
bounds the query but does not freeze the aggregates or guarantee a stable snapshot. For exports, reconcile overlapping queries using order and fill identifiers. Synthetic entries can share order_id 0, so do not deduplicate on order_id alone.

On this page
Export trade or funding history for an account. Supply both start_timestamp and end_timestamp in Unix milliseconds, or omit both for available history. If supplied, start_timestamp must be on or after 2025-01-01 UTC and earlier than end_timestamp. Exports are processed asynchronously; large histories may require smaller date ranges. The current implementation limits output to 40 GiB and processing to four hours; a completed export URL is valid for six hours.

https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/websocket.title: WebSocket
https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/websocket.content:
For the complete documentation index, see
llms.txt
. This page is also available as
Markdown
.
This page will help you get started with the Lighter WebSocket server.
Connection
Environment
URL
Lighter mainnet
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
Lighter testnet
wss://testnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
Robinhood Chain mainnet
wss://api.rh.lighter.xyz/stream
Robinhood Chain testnet
wss://api.rh-testnet.lighter.xyz/stream
You can directly connect to the WebSocket server using wscat:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
wscat
-c
'
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
'
If you're connecting from a restricted region, you can still access read-only data:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
wscat
-c
'
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream?readonly=true
'
Message envelope
Message
Meaning
type: "connected"
The socket is connected; subscribe to the channels you need.
type: "subscribed/<channel>"
Subscription acknowledgement with the initial snapshot.
type: "update/<channel>"
A subsequent update. Apply it according to that channel's rules.
error: {code, message}
Request or subscription failed. Errors need not contain a
type
field; an optional
id
identifies the request.
Subscribe requests use slash-separated channel names; response
channel
values use colons. Private channels take an
auth
token inside the subscribe message, as shown below. This WebSocket field is separate from REST authentication, which uses the
Authorization
header. Public-pool data does not require authentication; see
pool_data
and
pool_info
.
Structure blocks below use placeholders such as
INTEGER
,
STRING
and
FLOAT
; they describe payloads and are not literal JSON. Example response blocks are JSON.
transaction_time
is in microseconds and may be omitted when no transaction execution time is available. See
Timestamps
for field-specific units.
Keepalive Requirements
Clients are responsible for keeping the connection alive by sending at least one frame every
2 minutes
. This can be either:
A
WebSocket ping frame
Any application-level message
Clients sending
{"type":"ping"}
will receive back
{"type":"pong"}
.
If the server receives no frames from a client within the 2-minute window, it will close the connection.
Support for
permessage-deflate
compression is enabled.
Writes to slow clients time out after 250 ms by default. Keep reading messages continuously; if the connection closes, reconnect and resubscribe to obtain fresh snapshots.
Send Tx
You can send transactions using the websocket as follows:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "jsonapi/sendtx",
"data": {
"id": STRING, // returned in the ws response
"tx_type": INTEGER,
"tx_info": ...
}
}
The
tx_type
options can be found in the
SignerClient
file, while
tx_info
can be generated using the sign methods in the SignerClient.
Example:
create_modify_cancel_order_ws.py
Send Batch Tx
You can send batch transactions to execute up to 50 transactions in a single message. Larger batches are rejected with error
21514
.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "jsonapi/sendtxbatch",
"data": {
"id": STRING, // returned in the ws response
"tx_types": "[INTEGER]",
"tx_infos": "[tx_info]"
}
}
The
tx_type
options can be found in the
SignerClient
file, while
tx_info
can be generated using the sign methods in the SignerClient.
Example:
ws_send_batch_tx.py
Types
These types are shared across channels. Fields marked optional are omitted when zero or empty. Field names and numeric/string representations match the API.
Transaction JSON
To decode
event_info
, you can refer to
Data Structures
.

Ask

The order book channel sends the new ask and bid orders for the given market in batches, every 50ms. While the nonce is tied to Lighter's matching engine, the offset is tied to the API servers; hence, you can expect the offset to change drastically on reconnection if you're routed to a different server. Regardless, on each update the offset will increase, but it's not guaranteed to be continuous. Additionally, this channel sends a complete snapshot on subscription, but only state changes after that. To verify the continuity of the data, you can check that
begin_nonce
on the current update matches the
nonce
(i.e.
last_nonce
) of the previous update.

Copy

to

Notification
Provides notifications received by an account. Notifications can be of three kinds: liquidation, deleverage, or announcement. Each kind has a different content structure.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "subscribe",
"channel": "notification/{ACCOUNT_ID}",
"auth": "{AUTH_TOKEN}"
}
Response Structure
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"channel": "notification:{ACCOUNT_ID}",
"notifs": [
{
"id": STRING,
"created_at": STRING,
"updated_at": STRING,
"kind": STRING,
"account_index": INTEGER,
"content": NotificationContent,
"ack": BOOLEAN,
"acked_at": STRING
}
],
"type": "subscribed/notification"
}
Liquidation Notification Content
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"id": STRING,
"is_ask": BOOLEAN,
"usdc_amount": STRING,
"size": STRING,
"market_index": INTEGER,
"price": STRING,
"timestamp": INTEGER,
"avg_price": STRING
}

Average Entry Prices
Updates on the
account_spot_avg_entry_prices
channel are triggered whenever an event occurs for a given spot asset. Each event is accounted for as a buy or sell executed at the index price. Events include trades, deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and staking. The
last_trade_id
field confirms the validity of the data returned up to that
trade_id
.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "subscribe",
"channel": "account_spot_avg_entry_prices/{ACCOUNT_ID}",
"auth": "{AUTH_TOKEN}"
}
Example subscription:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "subscribe",
"channel": "account_spot_avg_entry_prices/1234",
"auth": "{AUTH_TOKEN}"
}
Response Structure:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"avg_entry_prices":{
"{ASSET_INDEX}":{
"asset_id":INTEGER,
"avg_entry_price":STRING,
"asset_size":STRING,
"last_trade_id":INTEGER
}
},
"channel":"account_spot_avg_entry_prices:{ACCOUNT_ID}",
"timestamp": INTEGER,
"type":"subscribed/account_spot_avg_entry_prices"
}
Example Response:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"avg_entry_prices":{
"1":{

}
},

"type":"subscribed/account_spot_avg_entry_prices"
}
Request for Quote (RFQ)
This channel allows you to receive all currently open RFQs, followed by live updates as new ones arrive. RFQ responses are hidden if you're not the requester, so you will only see the market and its size. API endpoints to create, respond, update, get, and list RFQs are available
here
. Currently, this program is whitelist-only.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "subscribe",
"channel": "rfq",
"auth": "{AUTH_TOKEN}"
}
Response Structure
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"channel":"rfq",
"rfqs":[
{
"id":INTEGER, // needed to respond
"account_index":INTEGER,
"market_index":INTEGER,
"direction":INTEGER, // redacted to -1
"base_amount":STRING,
"quote_amount":STRING,
"status":STRING,
"metadata":{},
"responses":[],
"created_at":INTEGER,
"updated_at":INTEGER
}
],
"type":"update/rfq"
}

"metadata":{
},
"responses":[
],
"created_at":1780077339117,
"updated_at":1780077339117
}
],
"type":"update/rfq"
}
